title: Token Spend Decomposition Explorer & Pricing Slab Composer
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Design a composable Console surface that lets engineers and finance teams decompose token spend by request slice, route, and model variant, and then author pricing slabs that map spend buckets to custom unit rates. The Explorer must support interactive breakdowns, attribution tracing (request -> prompt -> tokens -> billable bucket), CSV/JSON export with lineage metadata, and a compact pricing composer to preview invoice impact in-place.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive explorer UI that drills from product route -> prompt set -> token buckets with aggregated cost and percent contribution
Attribution trace that shows top N contributing prompts and can open the original prompt or request example in a side pane
Pricing Slab Composer UI to define up to 5 slab tiers, preview sample invoices using historical data, and validate against existing customer pricing rules
Export button produces CSV/JSON with request id, timestamp, route, prompt id, token counts, unit rate used, and computed line cost
Design annotated and handed to engineering with responsive assets, accessibility contrast checks, and microcopy for edge cases
tasks: Finalise information architecture for explorer (route, prompt, bucketing, pricing)
Prototype drill interactions in Figma and record click-through flows
Run 3 moderated usability sessions with platform teams and finance users
Address dev feedback and produce component spec for price-slab composer
Prepare handoff doc with acceptance criteria, data contract examples and export schema
design_decisions: Use progressive disclosure—top-level card shows aggregate spend with sparkline, clicking expands to prompt-level waterfall
Bucket tokens by billing unit (e.g., input vs output tokens) and by quantization/quant-profile impact as an optional column
Pricing Slabs are composable and order-sensitive; we show a live sample invoice for the last 30 days by default
Export format includes a stable request_trace_id to allow engineering to join exports back into logs and traces
Make attribution bounded to top 10 contributors to keep the view performant; add a ‘show more’ lazy-load for full lists
usability_feedback: Finance testers requested an 'effective rate' column (total cost / total tokens) — added to summary header
Platform engineers wanted a raw mode with no derived columns for validation; added a toggle
Design reviewers flagged potential confusion between 'route' and 'route+version' — changed label to 'route (version)'.
Accessibility review: color palette adjusted to meet 4.5:1 contrast for small numbers in charts
artifacts: Figma: Token Spend Decomposition Explorer (prototype) — page 'playground'
Handoff PDF: annotated spec + accessibility checklist
Prototype video: 4m click-through of slab composer and export
